A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the revised title and reordered appendices. Their main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 and Figures 2–3 report original synthetic logistic-regression and WideResNet28-10/CIFAR-10 experiments, including losses, classification errors, and variability across runs.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and their outcomes in Section 5 and Figures 2–3. Retained results still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The projected SGD updates, polynomial and cosine annealing schedules, and experimental averaging procedures are unchanged. The additional inverse-square-root analysis introduces no new proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic noisy binary-classification task and CIFAR-10 classification task. The additional mathematical counterexample does not introduce an experimentally evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: fixed stepsizes with the same averaging variants, cosine annealing, and linear decay, plus the same schedules in Figure 1. The inverse-square-root comparison added in v2 is theoretical, not an additional experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same geometric learning-rate grids, sub-grid selection procedure, metrics, sample sizes, and training settings. These include one epoch for logistic regression and 200 epochs for WideResNet28-10, with unchanged batching, momentum, weight decay, and averaging.

E4.justification: The numerical schedule-sensitivity analysis in Figure 1 and grid-resolution robustness experiments in Figures 2–3 are retained unchanged. No new ablation, empirical robustness test, or error analysis appears in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs per learning rate and report averages and standard deviations in Figures 2–3. Averaging across sub-grids is also unchanged, with no added uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 contain the same plotted results, and Section 5.2 retains the same numerical comparisons and qualitative findings. The added theoretical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds a substantive inverse-square-root schedule analysis, including a tuned upper bound and a counterexample yielding linear misspecification dependence for a uniformly random iterate and infinitely many individual iterates. This extends v1's fixed-stepsize analysis. v2 also permits zero averaging weights in Appendix B.1 and corrects a distance identity in Appendix A.1. The main annealing theorems remain unchanged. However, the new Section 2.2 remark omits 1/sqrt(T) in an intermediate equality.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed robustness contrast from fixed stepsizes to both fixed and inverse-square-root schedules. The central polynomial/cosine annealing guarantees and claims about coarse-grid empirical robustness are retained.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly discusses dependence on domain diameter D rather than the actual initial distance to the minimizer, quantifies the resulting penalty for linear decay, and explains when the guarantee remains informative. v2 also explains the restriction to stepsize overestimation. The experimental interpretations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed data-generation procedure, hyperparameters, scheduler-update frequencies, averaging parameter, SciPy numerical routines, and Wide ResNet implementation link are unchanged. No new hardware, runtime, code-release, or data-access information is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds Goujaud et al. (2022), Li et al. (2021), and Wu et al. (2022), positioning robustness alongside scheduling benefits for quadratic objectives, noise adaptation, and overparameterized regression. Other changes, including publication updates for Prodigy and Zamani–Glineur, concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially reorganized: v2 adds an approach overview, consolidates the contribution summary, moves the smooth reference guarantee from Section 2.2 to Section 4, and reorders all five appendices. It also adds a conclusion-and-limitations section, revises the title, and edits explanatory passages throughout.

P2.justification: All three figures retain their graphics. Figures 2–3 are placed together on one page, their separate a/b labels are replaced by left/right caption references, and captions are shortened. Several equations are reformatted or reflowed; no new figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: The added inverse-square-root counterexample, corrected proof identity, and explicit diameter-versus-initial-distance limitation improve theoretical context and transparency. The new overview also makes the retained argument easier to follow. These are limited overall gains because the central guarantees and experimental evidence remain unchanged. The missing 1/sqrt(T) factor in the new Section 2.2 remark is a localized mathematical defect that tempers the improvement.
